answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote on a task or claim rewards. The protocol weights influence by locked stake, not by account count, and destroys part of the deposit when an identity is proven to double-claim or collude. Splitting stake across a dune, a mesa, and an onyx of separate accounts therefore creates no extra influence; it only multiplies setup costs and exposes more capital to forfeiture.
